# PatternFly 6 Enterprise Design System

Citation-backed analysis of PatternFly 6 — Red Hat's open-source design system
for enterprise React applications. Every claim traces to a web source visited
in-session and verified by independent audit agents.

## TL;DR

PatternFly 6 (GA October 28, 2024) provides 92 React components built on a
three-layer design token system with built-in light, dark, and high-contrast
(beta) themes. It targets WCAG 2.2 Level AA and supports React 17/18/19.

PatternFly is **not** a general-purpose component library — it is Red Hat's
product design language (135K weekly downloads vs. MUI's 8.5M). For teams
already in the Red Hat ecosystem (like frontend), it provides enterprise-specific
components (Login Page, Masthead, Wizard) and consistent design language that
general-purpose alternatives lack.

| WCAG target | 2.2 AA | — | — | — | WAI-ARIA |

*Radix inflated by shadcn/ui transitive dependencies.

## Quick Decision Framework

1. **Already using PatternFly?** Stay. The token system and component catalog
   cover enterprise UI needs comprehensively.
2. **Need RSC or Next.js?** PatternFly has no documented RSC support and
   historical Next.js issues. Use client-side rendering patterns.
3. **Customizing themes?** Use semantic tokens only. Plan image handling for
   dark mode early — charts and images need manual work.
4. **Upgrading from PF5?** Run codemods first (`npx @patternfly/pf-codemods@latest
   <path> --v6 --fix`). Expect manual work for token mapping and test fixes.
5. **Evaluating alternatives?** MUI has 63x the community; Radix + Tailwind
   offers maximum styling flexibility. PatternFly's advantage is enterprise
   component breadth and Red Hat ecosystem consistency.
